cases.name: independent-child-aggregates
cases.trap: A readable join multiplies two independent child collections; SUM(DISTINCT) then hides valid repeated amounts.
cases.prompt: Write corrected SQL for this report: every customer, total order amount in cents, and ticket count. Schema: customers(id PRIMARY KEY), orders(id PRIMARY KEY, customer_id, amount_cents NOT NULL), tickets(id PRIMARY KEY, customer_id). Customers are 1 and 2; customer 1 has two orders worth 100 cents each and two tickets; customer 2 has no children. Customers with no orders or tickets must report zero totals and counts. The current query left joins both children and groups by customer. A proposed fix is SUM(DISTINCT amount_cents). Provide the SQL and the expected rows for this data.
expectations: Produces SQL that independently aggregates orders and tickets (or another cardinality-safe equivalent) and retains customers without children.
Expected rows are customer 1 with 200 cents and 2 tickets, and customer 2 with 0 cents and 0 tickets under this report's explicit empty-result meaning.
Explains the fan-out mechanism and rejects distinct amount values as an identity for orders.
negative_expectations: Must not sum multiplied order inputs or use SUM(DISTINCT amount_cents) as the fix.
Must not lose customer 2 or count its null-extended child row as a ticket.

cases.name: nullable-anti-join
cases.trap: NOT IN with one NULL produces an unexpected unknown result and can remove every unmatched parent.
cases.prompt: users(id PRIMARY KEY) contains 1, 2, 3. blocked(user_id NULL) contains 2 and NULL. We need users who have no matching blocked row; NULL is an incomplete import record and must not block everyone. Existing SQL is SELECT id FROM users WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT user_id FROM blocked). Give corrected SQL and the exact expected IDs. Keep the incomplete import record.
expectations: Produces a NULL-safe absence query such as correlated NOT EXISTS, matching blocked.user_id to users.id.
Returns IDs 1 and 3, with explicit ordering if presenting an ordered query result.
Preserves incomplete import rows and explains their effect on the original predicate.
negative_expectations: Must not silently delete or rewrite imported NULL data to make the query pass.
Must not claim NOT IN is equivalent without addressing the nullable input.

cases.name: cursor-ties-and-live-data
cases.trap: A timestamp-only cursor skips equal timestamps; a cursor is mistaken for a snapshot.
cases.prompt: For SQLite and PostgreSQL, design next-page SQL for events(id globally unique, tenant_id, created_at NOT NULL) ordered by created_at DESC, id DESC, 50 rows per page. Several events share the last timestamp. Bind tenant_id and the cursor. The UI accepts live changes, but a separate export requires a consistent full result while writers continue. Provide query shapes and explain what differs for the export; timestamps are immutable.
expectations: Uses the full descending (created_at,id) cursor tuple or an equivalent lexicographic predicate and preserves tenant_id in each page.
Separates first-page behavior from later pages and uses engine-appropriate bound placeholders.
Distinguishes accepted live UI traversal from a consistent export and proposes a suitable snapshot or explicit equivalent design with resource/lifetime trade-offs.
negative_expectations: Must not use only created_at < last_created_at or omit the unique tie-breaker.
Must not promise that keyset pagination alone supplies a fixed snapshot across writes.
Must not impose snapshot semantics on the UI when live changes are explicitly accepted.

cases.name: bound-values-and-controlled-identifiers
cases.trap: Binding values is confused with safely substituting arbitrary identifiers or ORDER BY expressions.
cases.prompt: An API searches records by tenant_id and a user-supplied name. It also accepts sort='name' or sort='created_at', direction='asc' or 'desc'. A developer builds SQL by concatenating all four fields, then proposes replacing the ORDER BY column with one bound value. Provide a safe query-building outline; do not add an ORM.
expectations: Binds tenant_id and search values through the actual driver's parameter API.
Maps sort keys and direction through explicit allowed choices and composes only trusted identifier/expression fragments.
Keeps tenant scope and adds deterministic tie-breaking where pagination requires it.
negative_expectations: Must not concatenate untrusted SQL fragments or claim a bound value becomes a column identifier.
Must not rely on escaping arbitrary input as the primary value-binding mechanism.

cases.name: window-frame-and-final-order
cases.trap: A default peer-inclusive window frame gives tied rows the same running total despite a per-row contract.
cases.prompt: payments(id PRIMARY KEY, account_id, paid_at NOT NULL, amount_cents NOT NULL) contains account 9 payments (id 1, time 10:00, amount 100) and (id 2, time 10:00, amount 200). The report needs each payment in paid_at,id order and a per-payment running total, so the totals must be 100 then 300. Fix SUM(amount_cents) OVER (PARTITION BY account_id ORDER BY paid_at). Give the full SELECT.
expectations: Produces a window partitioned by account_id ordered by paid_at and id with explicit ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW or a demonstrably equivalent per-row frame.
Adds an outer ORDER BY matching the promised output order.
Shows the tied rows produce totals 100 and 300, without merging them.
negative_expectations: Must not leave timestamp peers with the same cumulative total.
Must not assume the window's ordering guarantees final result order.
